nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الۤـمۤ. أَحَسِبَ ٱلنَّاسُ أَن يُتْرَكُوۤاْ أَن يَقُولُوۤاْ آمَنَّا وَهُمْ لاَ يُفْتَنُونَ﴾.
This is a question carrying the sense of affirmation and rebuke (taqrīr and tawbīkh): that is, do people think that they will be satisfied with merely saying "we believe", and not be tested so that the reality of their faith and their patience, their truthfulness and their lying, may be known and become manifest from them, and they be recompensed for it? As for the unseen, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, already knew it of them.
Then He said ﴿أَن يَقُولُوۤاْ آمَنَّا﴾, that is: on the basis that they say, and because they say, and by their saying, "we believe".
﴿وَهُمْ لاَ يُفْتَنُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: that is, they will not be put to trial.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾.
That is, We tried them.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ حَسِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلسَّيِّئَاتِ أَن يَسْبِقُونَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, that they will escape Us (yuʿjizūnā).

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَن كَانَ يَرْجُو لِقَآءَ ٱللَّهِ فَإِنَّ أَجَلَ ٱللَّهِ لآتٍ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the meaning is: whoever hopes to meet the reward of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَوَصَّيْنَا ٱلإِنْسَانَ بِوَالِدَيْهِ حُسْناً﴾.
That is, what is good.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِن جَاهَدَاكَ لِتُشْرِكَ بِي مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ فَلاَ تُطِعْهُمَآ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is: and if your parents strive against you, O man, to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, then do not obey them.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يِقُولُ آمَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ فَإِذَآ أُوذِيَ فِي ٱللَّهِ جَعَلَ فِتْنَةَ ٱلنَّاسِ كَعَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿فَإِذَآ أُوذِيَ فِي ٱللَّهِ﴾, that is, when he was tormented, he feared the torment of people as he fears the torment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: These were people who said "we believe", and when one of them was harmed he associated partners [with Allah].
Ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār from ʿIkrima, who said: "There were people in Mecca who had borne witness that "there is no god but Allah". When the idolaters went out to Badr, they compelled them to go out with them, and some of them were killed. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed concerning them: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَفَّاهُمُ المَلاَئِكَةُ ظَالِمي أَنْفُسِهِمْ قَالُوا فِيمَ كُنْتُمْ﴾ up to His saying ﴿فَأُوَلِئكَ عَسَى اللهُ أَنْ يَعْفُوَ عَنْهُمْ وكَانَ الله عَفُوَّاً غَفُورَاً﴾. The Muslims who were in Medina wrote it to the Muslims who were in Mecca. Then some Muslims went out of Mecca, the idolaters overtook them, and some of them succumbed to the trial; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed concerning them: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يِقُولُ آمَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ فَإِذَآ أُوذِيَ فِي ٱللَّهِ جَعَلَ فِتْنَةَ ٱلنَّاسِ كَعَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ﴾."
Al-Shaʿbī said: Ten verses were revealed concerning them, from His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿الم. أحَسِبَ النَّاسُ أَنْ يُتْرَكُوْا﴾. ʿIkrima said: The Muslims who were in Medina wrote them to the Muslims who were in Mecca. A man of Banū Ḍamra — who was ill — said: Take me out to relief (al-rawḥ). So they took him out, and he died; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed concerning him: ﴿وَمَنْ يَخْرُجْ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ مُهَاجِرَاً إلَى اللهِ وَرَسُوْلِهِ ثُمَّ يُدْرِكْهُ الْمَوْتُ فَقَدْ وقع أَجْرهُ عَلَى اللهِ﴾ to the end of the verse. And He revealed concerning the Muslims who had succumbed to the trial: ﴿ثم إنَّ ربَّكَ للَّذِينَ عملوا السُّوءَ بجهالةٍ ثم تابوا﴾ to the end of the verse.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱتَّبِعُواْ سَبِيلَنَا وَلْنَحْمِلْ خَطَايَاكُمْ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: These are the leaders of the idolaters.
Mujāhid said: They are the idolaters of the people of Mecca; they said to those of them who believed: Neither we nor you will be resurrected, so follow us, and if there is any burden of sin upon you, it is upon us.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is like your saying: "Put this on my neck if there is any sin in it", meaning: there is no sin in it.
Al-Farrāʾ said: It carries the sense of a conditional (mujāzāt), and he recited:
فقلْتُ ادْعِي وادْعُ فإنَّ أَنْدَى * لِصَوْتٍ أَنْ يُنَادَي دَاعِيانِ
(So I said: Call out, and let me call, for the farthest-carrying for a voice is that two callers cry out.)
He said: the meaning is "call, and let me call", that is: if you call, I will call.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا هُمْ بِحَامِلِينَ مِنْ خَطَايَاهُمْ مِّن شَيْءٍ﴾.
The meaning is: and they will not carry anything for them — that would lighten their load.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقَالَهُمْ وَأَثْقَالاً مَّعَ أَثْقَالِهِمْ﴾.
Abū Umāma al-Bāhilī said: "A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection with many good deeds, and retribution will continue to be taken from him until his good deeds are exhausted [and then claims are made against him]. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, will say: Take retribution from My servant. The angels will say: He has no good deeds left. He will say: Take from the bad deeds of the wronged one and put them on him."
Abū Umāma said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited ﴿وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقَالَهُمْ وَأَثْقَالاً مَّعَ أَثْقَالِهِمْ﴾.
Qatāda said concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿َوَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقَالَهُمْ وَأَثْقَالاً مَّعَ أَثْقَالِهِمْ﴾:
He said: "Whoever calls to misguidance, its burden is written against him, along with the burden of whoever acts by it, without that diminishing anything from theirs."
Abū Jaʿfar said: The people of exegesis hold that the meaning of the verse is as Qatāda said; and similar to it is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنْ أَوْزَارِ الَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلطُّوفَانُ وَهُمْ ظَالِمُونَ﴾.
Anything abundant that encompasses everyone — rain, killing or death — is called ṭūfān.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَخْلُقُونَ إِفْكاً﴾.
That is, and you carve.
The meaning on this view is: you only worship idols besides Allah, while you make them yourselves.
Mujāhid said: ﴿إفْكَاً﴾ means a lie.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān [al-Sulamī] read ﴿وتَخَلَّقُوْنَ إفْكاً﴾, and the meaning is the same.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَنتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَلاَ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: the meaning is: nor whoever is in the heaven; and "مَنْ" is indefinite. Someone else recited:
فَمَنْ يَهْجُو رسُوْلَ اللهِ مِنكُمْ * وَيَمْدحُهُ ويَنْصُرهُ سَوَاءُ
(Is the one of you who lampoons the Messenger of Allah, and the one who praises and supports him, alike?)
[Translator's note: the verse is cited for the omission of a second «مَنْ» before ويمدحه.]
Someone other than Abū al-ʿAbbās said the meaning is: you cannot escape [Him] on earth, even if you were in the heaven; and people were addressed in terms of what they know.
This is more fitting, and Allah knows best.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِ إِلاَّ أَن قَالُواْ ٱقْتُلُوهُ أَوْ حَرِّقُوهُ فَأَنْجَاهُ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾.
The meaning is: so they burned him, and Allah saved him from the fire.
It is related that it burned nothing but his bonds.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَآمَنَ لَهُ لُوطٌ وَقَالَ إِنِّي مُهَاجِرٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّيۤ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Abraham emigrated, and he was the first to emigrate.
Qatāda said: He emigrated from Kūthā to Syria (al-Shām).

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ أَجْرَهُ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
Sufyān related from Ḥumayd ibn Qays, who said: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr told a man to ask ʿIkrima about His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ أَجْرَهُ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
ʿIkrima said: The followers of all the religions claim him and say: He is one of us. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: He has spoken truly.
Qatāda said: It is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً﴾,
that is, well-being, righteous deeds and good praise; and that is because the people of every religion take him as their patron.
It has also been said: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ أَجْرَهُ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾ means that most of the prophets are from his offspring.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلُوطاً إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ إِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ ٱلْفَاحِشَةَ مَا سَبَقَكُمْ بِهَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِّنَ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
It is related that they were the first to mount men.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَئِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ ٱلرِّجَالَ وَتَقْطَعُونَ ٱلسَّبِيلَ﴾.
A question carrying the sense of rebuke and affirmation.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَقْطَعُونَ ٱلسَّبِيلَ﴾.
It has been said: they used to intercept people on the roads for wickedness.
It has also been said: that is, you cut off the way of offspring.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَأْتُونَ فِي نَادِيكُمُ ٱلْمُنْكَرَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: al-nādī is the assembly, and al-munkar (the abomination) is what they did with men.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-munkar in the language applies to obscene speech and to [obscene] action.
Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ibn al-Aswad narrated to us, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Marzūq narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bakr narrated to us, saying: Ḥātim ibn Abī Ṣaghīra narrated to us, from Simāk, from Abū Ṣāliḥ — the freedman of Umm Hāniʾ daughter of Abū Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with her — that she asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: I said, O Messenger of Allah, what about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَتَأْتُونَ فِي نَادِيكُمُ ٱلْمُنْكَرَ﴾: what was that abomination which they committed in their assembly? He said: They used to laugh at the passers-by and pelt them with pebbles.
Abū Jaʿfar said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, called this "an abomination" because people ought not to associate with one another in this way.
Usāma ibn Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥakam narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Bukayr, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَتَأْتُونَ فِي نَادِيكُمُ ٱلْمُنْكَرَ﴾: he said: They used to "yatafāʿalūna" in their gatherings, one of them doing it at another.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The shaykh said it with ḍād and ṭāʾ.
[Translator's note: the source writes the verb as the pattern word «يتفاعلون»; the remark that the shaykh pronounced it with ḍād and ṭāʾ indicates the actual word was «يتضارطون», i.e. they broke wind at one another.]

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّ فِيهَا لُوطاً قَالُواْ نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن فِيهَا﴾.
Abū Naṣr related from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samura, who said: Abraham ﷺ said to the angels: If there are a hundred among them who hate this, will you destroy them?
They said: No.
He said: And if there are ninety among them? They said: No.
Until he reached twenty. ﴿قَالَ إِنَّ فِيهَا لُوطاً﴾, the angels, may Allah bless them, said: ﴿نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن فِيهَا﴾. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: And they numbered four hundred thousand.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَمَّآ أَن جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَا لُوطاً سِيءَ بِهِمْ وَضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعاً﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, he thought ill of his people, and felt powerless on account of his guests.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is said ضِقْتُ به ذَرْعَاً, meaning "I could not bear it"; it is derived from al-dhirāʿ (the forearm), because strength lies in it.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَد تَّرَكْنَا مِنْهَآ آيَةً بَيِّنَةً لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿آيَةً بَيِّنَةً﴾ means a lesson.
Qatāda said: It is the stones that were left remaining.
Someone else said: a people of this community will be stoned with them.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِلَىٰ مَدْيَنَ أَخَاهُمْ شُعَيْباً﴾.
Qatāda said: Shuʿayb ﷺ was sent twice, to two nations: to the people of Madyan and to the Companions of the Thicket (al-Ayka).

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعَاداً وَثَمُودَاْ وَقَد تَّبَيَّنَ لَكُم مِّن مَّسَاكِنِهِمْ﴾.
That is, and We destroyed ʿĀd and Thamūd.
It has also been said: the implied wording (taqdīr) is: and remember ʿĀd and Thamūd.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَانُواْ مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, in error.
Qatāda said: that is, pleased with their error.
It has also been said: ﴿وَكَانُواْ مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ﴾ means they knew that they would be punished, and yet they did what they did.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمِنْهُم مَّن أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِ حَاصِباً﴾.
That is, ḥaṣab, which is stones; and they are the people of Lot.
﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّنْ أَخَذَتْهُ ٱلصَّيْحَةُ﴾: they are Thamūd and the people of Madyan.
﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّنْ خَسَفْنَا بِهِ ٱلأَرْضَ﴾: Qārūn and his companions.
﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّنْ أَغْرَقْنَا﴾: the people of Noah, and Pharaoh and his companions.
Then He, Exalted is He, informed that He did not wrong them in that, saying: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيَظْلِمَهُمْ وَلَـٰكِن كَانُوۤاْ أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْلِيَآءَ كَمَثَلِ ٱلْعَنكَبُوتِ ٱتَّخَذَتْ بَيْتاً﴾.
Qatāda said: This is a parable that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, struck; that is, it is of no benefit because of its weakness, just as the spider's house neither benefits nor protects.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّ أَوْهَنَ ٱلْبُيُوتِ لَبَيْتُ ٱلْعَنكَبُوتِ لَوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
﴿لَوْ﴾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to His saying ﴿مَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْلِيَآءَ كَمَثَلِ ٱلْعَنكَبُوتِ﴾: if only they knew that their patrons avail them nothing, and that this is their likeness.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلاَةَ إِنَّ ٱلصَّلاَةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ﴾.
Yūnus related from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever's prayer does not restrain him from indecency and abomination gains from it nothing but greater distance from Allah."
ʿAlī ibn Ṭalḥa related from Ibn Abī ʿAbbās, who said: In prayer there is a restraint and a deterrent from acts of disobedience.
[Translator's note: «ابن أبي عباس» is as written in the source; the usual chain is ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from Ibn ʿAbbās.]
Abū Jaʿfar said: It has been said that the meaning of this is: as long as the servant is in prayer, he is not engaged in indecency or abomination.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَذِكْرُ ٱللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَصْنَعُونَ﴾.
Sufyān related from Ibn Masʿūd, and related from Salmān, and from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَلَذِكْرُ ٱللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ﴾: they said: Allah's remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.
Ibn ʿAbbās added, after his words "of you": when you remember Him.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تُجَادِلُوۤاْ أَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَابِ إِلاَّ بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مِنْهُمْ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: Whoever fights you and does not give you the jizya, fight him with the sword.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda, who said: It is abrogated; it was abrogated by ﴿فَاقْتُلُوا المُشْرِكِين حَيْثُ وَجَدْتُمُوهُمْ﴾, and there is no disputation more severe than the sword.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of Qatāda is closer to being correct, because the surah is Meccan, and fighting was only commanded after the Hijra, and the taking of the jizya was commanded a long time after that; and moreover He said ﴿وَهُمْ صَاغِرُونَ﴾.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُولُوۤاْ آمَنَّا بِٱلَّذِيۤ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْنَا وَأُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ﴾.
Sufyān related from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, who said: "Some Jews used to sit with the Muslims and tell them things. The Prophet ﷺ was informed of this, and he said to them: Neither believe them nor disbelieve them, ﴿وَقُولُوۤاْ آمَنَّا بِٱلَّذِيۤ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْنَا وَأُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ to the end of the verse."

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كُنتَ تَتْلُواْ مِن قَبْلِهِ مِن كِتَابٍ وَلاَ تَخُطُّهُ بِيَمِينِكَ﴾.
And such is his description, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the Torah.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿إِذاً لاَّرْتَابَ ٱلْمُبْطِلُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Quraysh.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ هُوَ آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ فِي صُدُورِ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْعِلْمَ﴾.
There are three views on its meaning:
a- Al-Ḥasan said: Rather, the Qurʾan is clear signs in the breasts of the believers.
b- Qatāda said: Rather, the Prophet ﷺ is a clear sign; thus Qatāda read: "فِي صُدُوْرِ الَّذِينَ أُوْتُوا العِلْمَ، من أهل الكتاب" (in the breasts of those given knowledge, of the People of the Book).
c- Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: The description of the Prophet ﷺ was that he would not write with his right hand nor recite a book, and that is a clear sign.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِهِمْ أَنَّآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَابَ يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾.
Ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār from Yaḥyā ibn Jaʿda, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ was brought a shoulder-blade with writing on it, and he said: It is enough folly — or misguidance — for a people that they turn away from their prophet to a prophet other than him, or to a book other than their book." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِهِمْ أَنَّآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَابَ يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ (the verse).

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰعِبَادِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إِنَّ أَرْضِي وَاسِعَةٌ فَإِيَّايَ فَٱعْبُدُونِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: When you are commanded to commit acts of disobedience, flee.
ʿAṭāʾ said: When you see acts of disobedience, flee.
Mujāhid said: Emigrate and keep away from the idols.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The two views come back to one thing: Mujāhid's view is that they were commanded to emigrate and to shun the idol-worshippers. And the scholars said: likewise, when one is unable to enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, he should leave, and his ruling is the ruling of those.
It has also been said: that is, the land of Paradise is vast, so worship Me so that I may give it to you.

nahhas-meani:58-58.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ غُرَفَاً﴾.
That is, We will surely lodge them.
And the meaning of ﴿لَنُثْوِيَنَّهم﴾ is: We will surely give them dwellings in which they abide; it is said ثَوَى when one resides.
[Translator's note: ﴿لَنُثْوِيَنَّهم﴾ is a variant reading of ﴿لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ﴾; the source does not name its readers here.]

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَأَيِّن مِّن دَآبَّةٍ لاَّ تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: Birds and beasts do not carry their provision.
Al-Ḥumaydī related from Sufyān: ﴿لاَّ تَحْمِلُ﴾ means it does not store away. He said: Nothing stores up except man, the ant and the mouse.
Abū Jaʿfar said: ﴿دَآبَّةٍ﴾ applies to every living creature, rational and non-rational, except that its meaning here is restricted: that is, how many a helpless creature there is that Allah provides for, as well as you.

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلآخِرَةَ لَهِيَ ٱلْحَيَوَانُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: There is no death in it.
Qatāda said: al-ḥayawān is life.
Abū Jaʿfar said: One says ḥayawān, ḥayāh and ḥiyy, as [the poet] said:
* "وقد تَرَى إذِ الحَيَاةُ حِيُّ" *
(and you used to see, when life was alive…)
[Translator's note: the source has «قتال أبو جعفر», evidently a slip for «قال أبو جعفر».]

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا رَكِبُواْ فِي ٱلْفُلْكِ دَعَوُاْ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَ﴾.
That is, when hardship befalls them, they call on Allah alone and abandon what they worship besides Him.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى ٱلْبَرِّ إِذَا هُمْ يُشْرِكُونَ﴾.
That is, they call upon others along with Him.

nahhas-meani:66-66.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِيَكْفُرُواْ بِمَآ آتَيْنَاهُمْ وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُواْ فَسَوْفَ يَعلَمُونَ﴾.
﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُواْ﴾ is by way of threat, with kasra on the lām.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ جَاهَدُواْ فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾.
That is, We will surely increase them in guidance.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed us that He will help them, saying: ﴿وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَمَعَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾.
